statement:
For a ringed site (C,O), RSheafHom(L,M) is the internal derived Hom in D(O), contravariant in the first variable and covariant in the second. It may be represented by SheafHom^bullet(L^bullet,I^bullet) for any representative L^bullet of L and a **K-injective** representative I^bullet of M; equivalently it is right adjoint to −⊗^L_O L (source lines 8839–8869). Derived tensor uses K-flat replacements; the notation F|_U denotes exact restriction to the slice site C/U.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $L, M$ be objects
of $D(\mathcal{O})$. For every object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ we have
$$
H^0(U, R\SheafHom(L, M)) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O}_U)}(L|_U, M|_U)
$$
and we have $H^0(\mathcal{C}, R\SheafHom(L, M)) =
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O})}(L, M)$.
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site and all specified K,L,M are complexes of sheaves of O-modules, unless explicitly described as objects of the derived category D(O).
L,M∈D(O); no boundedness assumption is imposed.
conclusions: For L,M∈D(O) and every site object U, H^0(U,RSheafHom(L,M))≅Hom_{D(O_U)}(L|_U,M|_U), and H^0(C,RSheafHom(L,M))≅Hom_{D(O)}(L,M).

\label{lemma-section-RHom-over-U}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $L, M$ be objects

$$

$$
and we have $H^0(\mathcal{C}, R\SheafHom(L, M)) =

\label{lemma-restriction-RHom-to-U}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $K, L$ be objects
of $D(\mathcal{O})$. The construction of $R\SheafHom(K, L)$
commutes with restrictions, i.e.,

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $L$ be an
object of $D(\mathcal{O})$. Set $L^\vee = R\SheafHom(L, \mathcal{O})$.
For $M$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$ there is a canonical map
\begin{equation}
\label{equation-eval}
M \otimes^\mathbf{L}_\mathcal{O} L^\vee \longrightarrow R\SheafHom(L, M)
\end{equation}
which induces a canonical map
$$
H^0(\mathcal{C}, M \otimes_\mathcal{O}^\mathbf{L} L^\vee)
\longrightarrow
\Hom_{D(\mathcal{O})}(L, M)
$$
functorial in $M$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$.
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site and all specified K,L,M are complexes of sheaves of O-modules, unless explicitly described as objects of the derived category D(O).
conclusions: For L∈D(O), set L^vee=RSheafHom(L,O). For any M∈D(O), there is a natural evaluation map M⊗^L_O L^vee→RSheafHom(L,M), inducing after H^0 of global sections the map H^0(C,M⊗^L_O L^vee)→Hom_{D(O)}(L,M); no invertibility of the evaluation map is asserted.

which induces a canonical map
